text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT TRIGGERED - high RPM on model-family 'orion-7b' in prod-us-east. 5xx spike + token rate surge. current rolling RPM=18k, baseline=3k. paging eng-oncall @channel

anjali: taking this. oncall lead stepping in. quick question — is this traffic spread across API keys or one noisy key?

karim: looks like one-ish hotspot. logs show repeated short-gen calls from one key (api_k=ak_live_73). also seeing rising seq-lens but most requests small. suggest immediate per-model RPM cap and a hard per-key throttle.

matt: confirmed. kube-job for inference pool reporting high contended queues on p100 nodes, latency climbing. delta: KV cache miss rate up ~40%. suspect bursty fanout from single client.

support-cs: FYI, ACME-Corp reported 429s ~5 minutes ago. they say they retried aggressively. I can DM them to ask to back off if you want.

anjali: yes please DM them once we apply mitigation. mitigation plan: 1) temporarily lower ORION-7B RPM from 2000->800, 2) set per-key RPM cap for ak_live_73 to 200, 3) enable prefix KV caching policy for orion to reduce miss cost. execute now and observe for 15m.

karim: +1. prefer reducing RPM over fully disabling. also add a fallback to orion-7b-quantized variant if latency persists.

matt: running the commands now. posting admin calls below: 

```bash
# set per-model rpm cap
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/quotas/update" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model_family":"orion-7b","quota_type":"rpm","value":800,"reason":"auto mitigation - 1842501120 incident"}'

# set per-key throttle
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/keys/ak_live_73/throttle" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"rpm":200,"burst":50}'
```

matt: admin API returned 200 for both calls. changes in effect.

pagerduty-bot: UPDATE: mitigation applied by matt. incident status: mitigation_in_progress. notifying downstream dashboards.

matt: metrics coming in — overall RPM for orion family down to ~3.2k, 5xx rate decreasing. p99 latency back to acceptable band. KV cache hit improved after enabling prefix policy.

support-cs: messaged ACME-Corp, asked them to pause heavy workloads for 30m. they replied: "we're running a batch, throttling now".

anjali: nice. hold this for 30-45m and then slowly relax if stable. please add an incident note in PagerDuty with commands used & customer impacted. also add short-term action item: suspend auto-retries for that customer via support policy.

karim: filing an RFC item: auto-sculpting policy per-model that looks at per-key concentration and flips to stricter rpm/burst. will add to backlog.

matt: created a quick runbook snippet in the runbooks repo under orion-mitigation.md with the exact curl calls and observable playbook.

anjali: i'm handing off to jenna for nighttime watch. handoff: mitigation applied (rpm=800), ak_live_73 limited, ACME aware. keep an eye on orion family RPM >5k or 5xx >0.5% for >10m and page me + karim.

jenna: on it. thanks for the handoff — i'll monitor and escalate if thresholds cross. please ping in this thread if you see anything else.

anjali: summary for PD note: cause = concentrated noisy traffic from single customer -> resource contention -> KV cache miss spike -> degraded latency and 5xx. mitigation = per-model RPM reduced, per-key throttle applied, prefix caching enabled. customer contacted. monitoring in place.

matt: metrics stable for 12m. leaving dashboards pinned.

pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: metrics show stabilization. status: monitoring.

anjali: closing active mitigation window for now. leaving RPM at 800 for next 30m then gradual raise if stable. handing over to jenna for overnight. :white_check_mark:

jenna: acknowledged and will watch.

karim: postmortem assigned to matt + anjali + support-cs. deadline EOD tomorrow.

anjali: thanks team. great coordination.
